tools.description: Controls Unity Editor state (play/pause/resume/stop), synchronously imports changed project files with refresh, and retrieves current state. Refresh compiles code changes when required, clears Console, and returns the resulting Console errors and warnings. Use get_state whenever a decision requires a comprehensive current-state snapshot.

action.description: Action to perform. Use "get_state" for full state and "refresh" once per batch after changing project files outside Unity. Refresh automatically stops Play Mode (including paused play) — this discards all live runtime state — waits for Edit Mode before importing, and remains in Edit Mode afterward; tell the user before refreshing while they may be testing. Refresh synchronously imports changed assets, compiles code changes when required, clears Console, and returns the resulting Console errors and warnings. Use "pause" to pause and "resume" to resume play mode. Refresh and play/pause/resume/stop return only after the editor reaches the requested state.

timeoutSeconds.description: Client response budget in seconds for refresh and play mode operations

singleFrame.description: Required for resume: true to resume for one frame, false to resume continuously

Refresh automatically stops Play Mode (including paused play) — this discards all live runtime state — waits for Edit Mode before importing, and remains in Edit Mode afterward; tell the user before refreshing while they may be testing. Refresh synchronously imports changed assets, compiles code changes when required, clears Console, and returns the resulting Console errors and warnings. Use "pause" to pause and "resume" to resume play mode. Refresh and play/pause/resume/stop return only after the editor reaches the requested state.

tools.name: unity_editor

tools.description: Gets messages from, clears, or configures the Unity Editor console. Use set_collapse with collapse=true or false to persistently control Collapse. Supports filtering by message type, text content, and formatting options. There are no incremental reads: clear the console to establish a boundary, then read it.

scope.description: Scope for clear action: "all" clears everything (default), "errors_only" clears only error messages

count.description: Maximum number of messages to return

filterText.description: Text filter for messages (case-insensitive substring match)

sinceTimestamp.description: (DEPRECATED) Ignored by Unity. Incremental reads no longer exist: clear the console to establish a boundary, then read.

tools.name: unity_console

tools.description: Compile shader variants and preview a shader in the Editor. Write `.shader`, `.hlsl`, and `.compute` through an available file-writing path; when `exec_editor_script` is available, use `File.WriteAllText` + `AssetDatabase.ImportAsset`. Then call `unity_shader.compile` to compile them. Use an available material-assignment path (for example `exec_editor_script` + renderer.sharedMaterial) to assign a material that uses the shader to a renderer. Parameters: action, paths, shader_names, material_paths, variant_mode, keywords, include_passes, timeout_seconds, frames, mesh, resolution, material_path.

action.description: compile: reimport + variant warmup. Top-level success means the compile job finished; judge shader errors by error_count > 0 or has_errors, not success. Returns error_count, has_errors, and messages[]. preview: Editor PNG frames + is_error_pink. Preview animation uses _PreviewTime (not built-in _Time).

paths.description: For compile: asset paths starting with "Assets/". Accepts .shader files directly, or .hlsl/.cginc/.compute files (resolved to the .shader files that #include them).

shader_names.description: For compile/preview: shader internal names as declared in the Shader "Name/Path" block (e.g. "VFX/Ice"). Resolved via Shader.Find.

material_paths.description: For compile: material asset paths whose keyword state seeds variant compilation (variant_mode="used"/"common").

variant_mode.description: For compile: variant compilation scope. "used" = current material keywords only. "common" (default) = used + INSTANCING_ON/OFF + ShadowCaster + SRP default keywords. "explicit" = caller-supplied keyword combinations via keywords[][].

keywords.description: For compile with variant_mode="explicit": arrays of keyword combinations to compile, e.g. [["INSTANCING_ON"],["_MAIN_LIGHT_SHADOWS","INSTANCING_ON"]].

include_passes.description: For compile: pass names to include, e.g. ["ForwardLit","ShadowCaster"]. Defaults to Normal + ShadowCaster + ScriptableRenderPipeline.

timeout_seconds.description: For compile: optional timeout in seconds.

t.description: Time value written to the _PreviewTime float property for this frame. Shaders must read _PreviewTime; Unity's built-in _Time cannot be overridden in Editor preview.

props.description: Optional material property overrides for this frame. Values can be a number (float) or a 3/4-element array (vector).

frames.description: For preview: frames to render. Each entry specifies t (written to _PreviewTime) and optional per-frame property overrides. Defaults to [{t:0}]. Preview animation requires the shader to declare and use _PreviewTime.

mesh.description: For preview: built-in mesh to render the shader on. Defaults to "sphere".

resolution.description: For preview: output resolution in pixels (64–1024). Defaults to 256.

tools.name: unity_shader

tools.description: Manages Unity packages via UPM. install_package and remove_package return when the operation is finished. Can also list installed packages.

id_or_url.description: Package identifier (e.g., "com.unity.textmeshpro") or Git URL for install_package action

version.description: Optional version to install (e.g., "1.2.3"). Can also use format "package@version" in id_or_url.

timeoutSeconds.description: Timeout in seconds for the operation (default: 300)

tools.name: unity_package

tools.description: Handles NavMesh and Lighting baking operations. bake_navmesh and bake_lighting return when the bake is finished. Can also clear baked NavMesh and lighting data.

async.description: For bake_navmesh: use async UpdateNavMesh instead of synchronous BuildNavMesh. Requires existing NavMesh data on surfaces.

timeoutSeconds.description: Timeout in seconds for the operation (default: 600)

tools.name: unity_bake

tools.description: Execute Unity Editor menu items by their menu path or get available menus. Supports all Unity menu commands with safety blacklisting for dangerous operations. Use only for menu-only operations; never use it as the primary path for refresh, compilation, scene saving, or routine asset reimport. Asset reimport-related menu items (e.g., "Assets/Reimport", "Assets/Reimport All") are extremely heavy and should almost never be used by the model; prefer `unity_editor.refresh` once per batch, meta checks, and normal Unity import instead of menu-driven mass reimport.

menu_path.description: Full menu path separated by forward slashes (e.g., "File/Save Project", "GameObject/Create Empty", "Assets/Reimport All"). Can use snake_case or camelCase.

menuPath.description: Alternative camelCase naming for menu_path. Full menu path separated by forward slashes.

action.description: Action to perform: "execute" to run menu item, "get_available_menus" to list available menus

parameters.description: Optional parameters for the menu item (rarely used for most menu commands). Future feature.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds (future feature, currently not used)

alias.description: Menu path alias for common operations (future feature)

tools.name: unity_menu

tools.description: Captures Unity Editor output for final visual verification. Prefer non-visual evidence for routine checks. Native Game View MP4 recording is supported on Windows and macOS, not Linux. On supported platforms, use exec_runtime_script.record_game_view for dynamic effects that the same script can trigger or restart; use start_game_view_recording / finish_game_view_recording only for input or external events after Play Mode is active. If MP4 reports unsupported, capture an animated GIF or multi-frame image during the effect and combine it with structured runtime evidence; one static frame does not prove time-varying behavior. Direct static Game View capture is disabled. Never call capture_main_camera or capture_specific_camera in Play Mode unless the user explicitly requested genuinely static output and you provide allow_static_in_play_mode=true with a specific static_reason.

action.description: Capture action. Static Edit Mode: capture_scene_view/capture_scene_camera, capture_main_camera, capture_specific_camera, capture_asset, capture_ui_toolkit. Never use capture_main_camera or capture_specific_camera in Play Mode for time-varying output. Dynamic MP4 (Windows/macOS only): use exec_runtime_script.record_game_view to enter Play automatically and trigger or restart the effect. start_game_view_recording requires Play Mode already and is only for input or external events that cannot be restarted from a script; finish_game_view_recording waits for encoding. On unsupported platforms such as Linux, use an animated GIF or multi-frame capture plus structured runtime evidence. capture_game_view and its legacy capture alias are disabled.

path.description: [All capture/start actions] Optional custom output directory. Defaults to <ProjectRoot>/screenshots. Game View MP4 recording paths must stay inside the current Unity project.

filename.description: [All capture/start actions] Optional custom filename. The appropriate image or .mp4 extension is added when needed; a timestamped name is generated when omitted. MP4 recording accepts a file name only, not a path or "..".

width.description: [capture_scene_view | capture_main_camera | capture_specific_camera | capture_asset | capture_ui_toolkit] Output width in pixels. Defaults: cameras use their pixel width; others default to 1024.

height.description: [capture_scene_view | capture_main_camera | capture_specific_camera | capture_asset | capture_ui_toolkit] Output height in pixels. Defaults: cameras use their pixel height; others default to 1024.

camera_name.description: [capture_specific_camera —REQUIRED] Name of the camera GameObject to render. The camera is located by exact name match (case-insensitive).

view.description: [capture_scene_view | capture_asset] Camera direction(s) to render. current is default; "cardinal" = front + right + top + iso stitched into a grid; "all" = all 7 directions; any other value renders a single direction.

render_mode.description: [capture_scene_view] How geometry is drawn: "shaded" (default) = normal lit/textured; "wireframe" = wireframe only; "shadedwireframe" = shaded surfaces with wireframe edges overlaid. Only applies to capture_scene_view.

over_time.description: [capture_scene_view | capture_main_camera | capture_specific_camera] Multi-frame capture. Format: "N" captures N frames; "NxS" captures N frames with S simulation steps between each. Frames are stitched into a grid. Example: "4x1" = 4 frames, 1 step apart. Ignored when as_gif is set (GIF capture takes precedence).

orthographic.description: [capture_scene_view | capture_asset] Use orthographic projection instead of perspective (default: false).

assets.description: [capture_asset —REQUIRED] Asset paths to instantiate and render (e.g. ["Assets/Prefabs/Hero.prefab"]). Supports GameObject/Prefab, Mesh, Material, Texture2D, Sprite. Multiple assets are laid out side-by-side and captured together.

scene.description: [capture_asset —optional] Path to a .unity scene file (e.g. "Assets/Scenes/Preview.unity"). When provided the scene is opened additively, assets are staged inside it, and the scene is closed after capture. Without this parameter assets are staged in the currently active scene.

document_path.description: [capture_ui_toolkit —REQUIRED] Path to the .uxml VisualTreeAsset (e.g. "Assets/UI/HUD.uxml"). Requires Unity 2021.2 or newer.

focusobject.description: Hierarchy path of the target GameObject (e.g. "Root/Player"). Segments separated by "/".

index.description: Zero-based sibling index to disambiguate when multiple children share the same name at the final path segment (default: 0).

focus_object.description: [capture_scene_view —optional] Frame the Scene View camera on a specific GameObject instead of the whole scene bounds before capturing.

scale.description: [start_game_view_recording] Resolution scale factor applied to recorded Game View frames (default 0.5).

as_gif.description: [capture_scene_view | capture_main_camera | capture_specific_camera] When true, records multiple frames and saves an animated .gif instead of a PNG. Capture is paced to fps and frameCount is REQUIRED. Takes precedence over over_time (over_time is ignored). Not applicable to capture_asset or capture_ui_toolkit. Estimated size at 480x270: ~200KB/frame (e.g. 100 frames ≈ 3MB). Maximum output: 15MB.

fps.description: [as_gif] Playback frame rate (10-30, default 25). [start_game_view_recording] Capture frame rate: how many frames per second are grabbed from the Game View (5-30, default 15). Higher values capture more visual detail.

encodeFps.description: [start_game_view_recording] MP4 metadata frame rate (1-30). Defaults to fps (normal speed). Set to 2 for slow-motion when this recording is the final visual gate for VLM video verification — a 2fps-sampling model (e.g. GLM) will then see every captured frame instead of skipping most.

startDelay.description: [as_gif | start_game_view_recording] Seconds to wait before capture starts (0-5, default 0).

durationSeconds.description: [start_game_view_recording] MP4 recording duration in seconds (1-8, default 5). Requires Play Mode already. For an effect you can trigger or restart from a script, use exec_runtime_script.record_game_view; it enters Play automatically. This split action is only for input or external events that cannot be restarted from a script.

recording_id.description: [finish_game_view_recording —REQUIRED] Recording ID returned by start_game_view_recording. Always pass the returned ID so another caller cannot collect the wrong active recording.

allow_static_in_play_mode.description: [capture_main_camera | capture_specific_camera] Explicit Play Mode override for genuinely static output only. Time-varying output needs multi-frame evidence. Requires static_reason.

static_reason.description: [allow_static_in_play_mode] Required explanation of why one frame is sufficient. The user must have explicitly requested static Play Mode output.

tools.name: unity_screenshot

tools.description: Gets, sets, and lists the Unity Game View resolution. set_resolution selects an existing fixed resolution or creates one when missing.

action.description: Game View operation: "get_resolution" – return the currently selected resolution; "set_resolution" – select (creating if needed) a fixed width×height resolution; "list_resolutions" – list every resolution in the current size group.

width.description: [set_resolution – REQUIRED] Target width in pixels. Must be between 1 and 8192.

height.description: [set_resolution – REQUIRED] Target height in pixels. Must be between 1 and 8192.

tools.name: unity_gameview

tools.description: Get the authoritative 32-character hex guid that scene, prefab, and asset YAML use to reference an asset. Tuanjie .meta files store an encrypted guid instead; pass the asset path (the .meta path without the .meta suffix) and the running editor resolves the real guid through AssetDatabase.AssetPathToGUID. Optionally pass guid to verify the asset: a 32-character hex guid is compared with the YAML guid, any other value with the encrypted guid in the .meta file; a mismatch returns an error. This tool does not guess or locally decrypt guids.

asset_path.description: Project-relative asset path under Assets/ or Packages/, such as Assets/Scripts/TestEmpty.cs or Packages/com.example/package.json

guid.description: Optional guid to verify: the encrypted guid from the .meta file or an expected 32-character hex guid

tools.name: unity_guid

tools.description: Queries and cancels in-flight Unity bridge jobs. Handled on a background thread in the Unity editor, so it works even while the main thread is busy or blocked. Actions: status/check (poll a job by id; a finished result is returned exactly once), list (all in-flight jobs), cancel (request cancel by job id — applied on the next runner tick). When a response reports a job as detached (e.g. because a modal dialog blocked the editor), use action "status" with the job id to query its state and collect the result.

action.description: Job operation to perform (check is an alias of status)

job_id.description: Job id from a detached/pending response (required for status/check/cancel)

reason.description: Optional reason for cancel (defaults to "client aborted")

tools.name: unity_job

tools.description: Clicks a button on a native modal dialog that is blocking the Unity editor main thread. Handled on a background thread in the editor, so it works while the dialog has the editor frozen. When such a dialog appears, its notification and detached-job reason list its title, message, and button labels. Choose one of those labels (param "button" is a regex over the button labels, optional "title" filters by dialog title) and click it with this tool. Then retry the original command; for detached jobs, use unity_job (action "status") to collect their results.

button.description: Regex matched against the dialog button labels; the first matching button is clicked

title.description: Optional regex matched against dialog titles to pick which dialog to click

tools.name: unity_dialog

tools.description: Executes a custom Unity tool by name. Custom tools are registered in Unity Editor via C# attributes or tool providers. Use this for user-defined or plugin-provided tools not covered by built-in Unity tools.

tool_name.description: Name of the custom tool to execute. Must match a registered tool name in Unity.

parameters.description: Parameters to pass to the custom tool. Structure depends on the specific tool.

tools.name: execute_custom_tool

tools.description: Executes C# automation in Unity Edit Mode using Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Scripting. The tool automatically exits Play Mode (discarding any live runtime state) and waits for the transition before executing; when the user may be testing, tell them before calling. Use it for project settings, scene setup and authoring, Animation/Animator editing, AssetDatabase, EditorSceneManager, prefabs, and other UnityEditor APIs. Supports independent one-shot calls. It must not block the Unity main thread. For a complete task, normally make iterative Edit Mode adjustments with this tool, save, call unity_editor.refresh once per batch when project files changed, then use exec_runtime_script for Play Mode behavior and dynamic visual verification. Do not call unity_editor stop before this tool; mode switching is automatic. Inspect unverified APIs in a separate read-only query or current source before use.

script.description: Inline C# script code to execute. The legacy script_path parameter is not exposed. The script runs on the Unity main thread and must never block it: do not use Thread.Sleep, Thread.SpinWait, Task.Wait, Task.Result, .WaitOne() on synchronization primitives, or busy-wait loops. Top-level await is invalid; wrap asynchronous work in a local async function and return its Task. Top-level yield return is not valid Roslyn script syntax. For multi-frame work, define a local method returning IEnumerator and return that IEnumerator. Returned coroutines may yield null, WaitForSeconds, WaitForSecondsRealtime, WaitUntil, WaitWhile, WaitForEndOfFrame, WaitForFixedUpdate, or nested IEnumerators.

summary.description: A concise, one-line summary of the script goal, not its implementation.

capture_logs.description: Whether to capture Unity logs during script execution. Default: true.

timeoutSeconds.description: Deadline for returned Task or IEnumerator work in seconds. Omitted uses the Bridge default (300); positive values are capped at 3600; 0 opts into no Bridge deadline.

backup_paths.description: Relative .cs paths this script will overwrite (e.g. "Assets/Scripts/Foo.cs"). Read and backed up before the script runs so rewind can restore them. Only .cs files.

tools.name: exec_editor_script

tools.description: Executes C# behavior checks and interactions in Unity Play Mode using Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Scripting. The tool automatically enters Play Mode and waits for the transition before executing. Use it for runtime state inspection, gameplay interactions, behavior tests, Task/IEnumerator multi-frame work, and dynamic visual verification. Pass record_game_view when the same script can trigger or restart a short-lived effect; recording begins atomically before user code runs. It must not block the Unity main thread. Complete Edit Mode authoring first with exec_editor_script, then use this tool for runtime testing. Do not call unity_editor play before this tool; mode switching is automatic. Inspect unverified APIs in a separate read-only query or current source before use.

script.description: Inline C# script code to execute. The legacy script_path parameter is not exposed. The script runs on the Unity main thread and must never block it: do not use Thread.Sleep, Thread.SpinWait, Task.Wait, Task.Result, .WaitOne() on synchronization primitives, or busy-wait loops. Top-level await is invalid; wrap asynchronous work in a local async function and return its Task. Top-level yield return is not valid Roslyn script syntax. For multi-frame work, define a local method returning IEnumerator and return that IEnumerator. Returned coroutines may yield null, WaitForSeconds, WaitForSecondsRealtime, WaitUntil, WaitWhile, WaitForEndOfFrame, WaitForFixedUpdate, or nested IEnumerators.

summary.description: A concise, one-line summary of the script goal, not its implementation.

capture_logs.description: Whether to capture Unity logs during script execution. Default: true.

timeoutSeconds.description: Deadline for returned Task or IEnumerator work in seconds. Omitted uses the Bridge default (300); positive values are capped at 3600; 0 opts into no Bridge deadline.

fps.description: Capture frame rate: how many frames per second are grabbed from the Game View. Higher values capture more visual detail.

encodeFps.description: MP4 metadata frame rate. Defaults to fps (normal speed). Set to 2 for slow-motion when the recording is the final visual gate for VLM video verification — a 2fps-sampling model (e.g. GLM) will then see every captured frame instead of skipping most. Example: 5s @ capture 15fps + encode 2fps → 75 frames in a 37.5s slow-motion MP4; a 2fps model samples all 75.

path.description: Optional output directory inside the current Unity project. Defaults to <ProjectRoot>/screenshots.

filename.description: Optional MP4 file name only; directories, absolute paths, and ".." are rejected.

record_game_view.description: Optional atomic Game View MP4 recording (Windows/macOS only). Recording starts immediately before the runtime script, so trigger the effect in that script. On Linux, use multi-frame evidence instead.

tools.name: exec_runtime_script

tools.description: Access the Unity developer experience wiki. Discover categories, list their articles, and read articles by ID.

action.description: Action to perform. Use "list_categories" to discover categories, "list_category" to list articles, and "read_article" to read an article.

articleId.description: For action "read_article". Article ID in format "{category}/{filename}".

tools.name: unity_wiki
